references.text: The parallel passage in Matthew where John's disciples tell him about Christ's deeds, and John sends two of them to ask Jesus if he is the one who was to come.
The preceding verses describe the mighty works Jesus performed—raising the widow's son at Nain and other healings—which are 'all these things' (περὶ πάντων τούτων) that were reported to John.
John had been thrown into prison by Herod, which explains why he depended on his disciples coming to tell him about Jesus' deeds.
John's disciples had come to him with questions about Jesus before, showing that they kept watch over Jesus' ministry and reported back to their master.
The immediate result of John hearing all this was that he sent two of his disciples to Jesus with the question of whether he was the one who was to come.
